title: Constellation Hotels takes back its Paris flagship
why: Owners of trophy assets increasingly want to control the brand, not just the walls. A new luxury operator is born from The Connaught, The Berkeley and The Emory.

body_long:
Paris is about to gain a new luxury hotel operator, and it starts with one of the city's most anticipated projects. Constellation Hotels, now sole owner of the former Maybourne Saint-Germain, is taking back the management and branding of the hotel on boulevard Saint-Germain, Hospitality ON reported on 15 October 2026.

## What changed

At the end of August, two cousins from Qatar's ruling Al-Thani family split the assets that had been managed by the Maybourne group. Constellation Hotels became the sole owner of the Paris project, and of three operating London hotels: The Connaught, The Berkeley and The Emory. The Maybourne name, however, stays with the other side, through Regis Maybourne Ltd. Constellation therefore needs a new name for its Paris hotel. According to CFNEWS IMMO, it will be called Le Saint-Germain; this has not yet been confirmed by the owner.

The project converts a former government building on the Left Bank into a luxury hotel, with total costs estimated at more than €300 million. Works are continuing and the owner does not appear to plan a sale. As with the other former Maybourne hotels, Maybourne is expected to keep operating the property for a period under a management contract.

## A new operator

Constellation is led by Gianluca Muzzi, former co-CEO of Maybourne. Like many owners of trophy assets, it is building its own management platform. In September it hired Neil Jacobs, the former CEO of Six Senses, to lead the new operator. Jacobs has said a new brand collection will be unveiled before the end of 2026, focused on quality, warmth and a sense of joy.

## The signal

Owners of trophy assets increasingly want to control the brand, not just the walls. A new luxury operator born from three of London's most celebrated hotels, with Paris as an early flagship, is one to watch. For the Paris market, it also means one more ultra-luxury opening on the Left Bank in the coming years, with a leadership team that knows the city's palaces well.

We will follow the new brand's unveiling closely.
